    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, the midterm postmortem will continue for some time. Conservatives need careful data analysis from people who can interpret the numbers and understand politics, and politicians who can respond to public opinion with prudence and guiding rhetoric.But as The Daily Wire hosts noted, there is an even deeper problem that needs attention: no one has made a “robust argument for Americanism as an argument, a fully fleshed out argument.” What are the values that make America, America? What is the positive vision?America as a nation is defined by the organic intertwining of people, place, and principles. Each contributes something unique, and they reinforce one another to form a whole even greater than the sum of its parts.James Madison’s theory of separation of powers and checks and balances provides a helpful analogy. Each branch of government has particular responsibilities, but they are not strictly divided from one another. Instead, each branch holds pieces of the others. The president, for example, has the power to veto legislation, giving the executive branch a legislative function. With this dynamic, the three branches check each other to ensure that all act with fidelity and cohere as a single entity.>>> How To Win Back the Disillusioned American DreamThe same is true of the American nation of people, place, and principles.PeopleAmerica is a people sustained over generations by what Americans hold in common: language, history, traditions, and religion, to name a few. As John Jay wrote in Federalist 2:Providence has been pleased to give this one connected country to one united people—a people descended from the same ancestors, speaking the same language, professing the same religion, attached to the same principles of government, very similar in their manners and customs, and who, by their joint counsels, arms, and efforts, fighting side by side throughout a long and bloody war, have nobly established general liberty and independence.A shared culture binds Americans together and supports American principles. For example, speaking the same language allows neighbors to interact, thereby building goodwill and friendship. Communication also enables civic participation and deliberation, which are necessary for self-government.Religious institutions have historically played a major role in that deliberation. Churches are gathering places and seedbeds for community activity; they are the most vital civic associations. At the time of the Founding, 70–80% of American colonists attended services regularly, and the ideas of the Revolution, consistent with biblical principles, spread through sermons, pamphlets, and newspapers.Religion is not the only way a people sustain itself. As George Washington wrote in his Farewell Address, an individual can develop a moral framework independently, but “reason and experience both forbid us to expect that National morality can prevail in exclusion of religious principle.” The Founders and ancient philosophers alike argued that a republic cannot survive without a virtuous people, and religious belief and practice are indispensable for morality.PlaceHuman embodiment comes with an instinctive love of home. America’s physical wonders and gifts inspire awe and gratitude. A sense of reverence reigns over the places where many of our ancestors gave the last full measure of their devotion. And fondness builds in the communities where Americans practice civic rituals and raise posterity. These attachments are good and serious.Yet America as a place is even more: it has fostered American principles and formed the national character.From the outset, James Madison argued that America’s extended territory mitigates the problem of faction: groups adverse to the common good. America has numerous factions, which makes it harder for any single faction to gain a majority. Instead, people and representatives must work with one another and communicate to achieve their goals. That deliberative process slows things down and makes it more likely that justice will prevail.John Jay further observed that America was composed not of “detached and distant territories” but of “one connected, fertile, wide-spreading country” with a “succession of navigable waters” almost made “to bind it together.” The Founders’ response to America as a place was consistent with democratic principles and reinforced the sovereignty of the people.Through the Potomac River Project, which connected regions by roads and waterways, George Washington sought to bind the nation and the character of the American people. Thomas Jefferson led the repeal of primogeniture and entail laws in Virginia. The Northwest Ordinance of 1787 extended that vision to the frontier, and the taming of America’s heartland was given over to those who would steward the land, rather than left to be worked by the many and owned by a few aristocrats.The frontier spirit is part of the American heritage as a result. Americans are adventurous, informal, resilient, industrious, and somewhat gritty. Both the yeoman farmer and the entrepreneur animate the American moral imagination, as America’s physical resources, free institutions, and the human capacity for creativity unleashed profound prosperity.PrinciplesAmerica is the experiment in self-government, and self-government has a multi-layered meaning.Self-government at the institutional level means republican government, in which the people have a real say in the nation’s laws through mechanisms such as popular elections. As James Madison wrote, “no other form” of government “would be reconcilable with the genius of the people of America; with the fundamental principles of the Revolution; or with that honorable determination which animates every votary of freedom, to rest all our political experiments on the capacity of mankind for self-government.”As Madison suggests, self-government at the individual level underlies republican government. Because human beings have reason and conscience, they are responsible for their actions and can order reason above their passions and impulses.The maxim “all men are created equal” expressed in the Declaration of Independence recognizes the nature of human beings and situates mankind in an ordered universe. As John Adams wrote:[Equality] really means little more than that We are all of the same Species: made by the same God: possessed of Minds and Bodies alike in Essence: having all the same Reason, Passions, Affections and appetites. All Men are Men and not Beasts…. The blind are Men, and not Insects, the deaf are Men and not reptiles, the dumb are Men and not Trees. All these are Men and not Angells…America as a nation is dedicated to these principles, which define the American national character.As distinguished Washington and Founding scholar Dr. William B. Allen has written, Lincoln and others believed that regimes are guided by “a shared view of justice that makes a people a people. This was a very old idea, one expressed by Plato, and Aristotle, and Cicero, and Aquinas, and even Jefferson.”Shared understanding imposes limits on behavior and introduces the possibility of friendship, love, and goodwill. As a people, Americans have declared that “life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness” are inalienable rights, and that rights and duties are non-negotiable. Citizens can reasonably take for granted that neighbors will not use force or steal one another’s property, and those boundaries allow interaction and harmony.ConclusionArticulating a positive vision of the American nation helps identify policy solutions and cultural difficulties.Challenges to self-government include the growth of the administrative state and the erosion of deliberation by instant communication.>>> Freedom Isn’t Automatic—Each Generation Must Fight To Keep ItThis customizable and disembodied world erodes shared memories and experiences. Americans are less likely to gather for small-town parades and fireworks, as spending a solitary evening of Netflix and Uber Eats is more comfortable than eating a hot dog with a neighbor. For such reasons, preserving and defending the physical historic sites that transmit the American story and bring citizens together is even more urgent.Political and legal decisions have driven religion out of the public square, and churches have lost parishioners as they have diluted doctrine and required less of the human person.Immigration remains a concern as insular communities fail to assimilate into the American way of life. Explaining why others should assimilate requires educating the native-born population in the nation’s Founding principles, so its members can articulate why America is exceptional and worthy of loyalty.The nation’s Founding story teaches Americans who they are: a people committed to the principles of self-government, rights and duties, human equality, and the dictates of the natural order.These are just a few solutions that would reinforce people, place, and principles. Clarity about what constitutes the American nation guides policy prescriptions. Establishing that clarity is a necessary step in responding to the midterms.

    Through the Potomac River Project, which connected regions by roads and waterways, George Washington sought to bind the nation and the character of the American people. Thomas Jefferson led the repeal of primogeniture and entail laws in Virginia. The Northwest Ordinance of 1787 extended that vision to the frontier, and the taming of America’s heartland was given over to those who would steward the land, rather than left to be worked by the many and owned by a few aristocrats.

    The frontier spirit is part of the American heritage as a result. Americans are adventurous, informal, resilient, industrious, and somewhat gritty. Both the yeoman farmer and the entrepreneur animate the American moral imagination, as America’s physical resources, free institutions, and the human capacity for creativity unleashed profound prosperity.

    Principles.

    America is the experiment in self-government, and self-government has a multi-layered meaning.

    Industry observers note that self-government at the institutional level means republican government, in which the people have a real say in the nation’s laws through mechanisms such as popular elections. As James Madison wrote, “no other form” of government “would be reconcilable with the genius of the people of America; with the fundamental principles of the Revolution; or with that honorable determination which animates every votary of freedom, to rest all our political experiments on the capacity of mankind for self-government.”.

    It has been revealed that as Madison suggests, self-government at the individual level underlies republican government. Because human beings have reason and conscience, they are responsible for their actions and can order reason above their passions and impulses.

    The maxim “all men are created equal” expressed in the Declaration of Independence recognizes the nature of human beings and situates mankind in an ordered universe. As John Adams wrote:.

    It has been revealed that [Equality] really means little more than that We are all of the same Species: made by the same God: possessed of Minds and Bodies alike in Essence: having all the same Reason, Passions, Affections and appetites. All Men are Men and not Beasts…. The blind are Men, and not Insects, the deaf are Men and not reptiles, the dumb are Men and not Trees. All these are Men and not Angells….

    America as a nation is dedicated to these principles, which define the American national character.

    Sources indicate that as distinguished Washington and Founding scholar Dr. William B. Allen has written, Lincoln and others believed that regimes are guided by “a shared view of justice that makes a people a people. This was a very old idea, one expressed by Plato, and Aristotle, and Cicero, and Aquinas, and even Jefferson.”.

    Shared understanding imposes limits on behavior and introduces the possibility of friendship, love, and goodwill. As a people, Americans have declared that “life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness” are inalienable rights, and that rights and duties are non-negotiable. Citizens can reasonably take for granted that neighbors will not use force or steal one another’s property, and those boundaries allow interaction and harmony.

    Conclusion.

    Articulating a positive vision of the American nation helps identify policy solutions and cultural difficulties.

    Challenges to self-government include the growth of the administrative state and the erosion of deliberation by instant communication.

    >>> Freedom Isn’t Automatic—Each Generation Must Fight To Keep It.

    Recent findings suggest that this customizable and disembodied world erodes shared memories and experiences. Americans are less likely to gather for small-town parades and fireworks, as spending a solitary evening of Netflix and Uber Eats is more comfortable than eating a hot dog with a neighbor. For such reasons, preserving and defending the physical historic sites that transmit the American story and bring citizens together is even more urgent.

    Political and legal decisions have driven religion out of the public square, and churches have lost parishioners as they have diluted doctrine and required less of the human person.

    Immigration remains a concern as insular communities fail to assimilate into the American way of life. Explaining why others should assimilate requires educating the native-born population in the nation’s Founding principles, so its members can articulate why America is exceptional and worthy of loyalty.

    The nation’s Founding story teaches Americans who they are: a people committed to the principles of self-government, rights and duties, human equality, and the dictates of the natural order.

    These are just a few solutions that would reinforce people, place, and principles. Clarity about what constitutes the American nation guides policy prescriptions. Establishing that clarity is a necessary step in responding to the midterms.

    COP31 Failed Climate-Displaced Communities

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (415 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Hrw

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Leaving the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, I can’t shake the disconnect between the reality of entire communities losing their homes to rising seas and some governments’ apathy and obstruction of the process.
    • In a recent development, I am still in awe of Francis, a community leader from Solomon Islands who traveled to Antalya to share his story.
    • Recent findings suggest that COP31’s inability to reach an overarching agreement leaves communities like Walande—and hundreds of other communities that have been forced to relocate—to face consequences of the climate crisis on their own.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Leaving the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, I can’t shake the disconnect between the reality of entire communities losing their homes to rising seas and some governments’ apathy and obstruction of the process. The conference ended without consensus on the proposed Antalya Pact—the overarching political agreement for the COP31 climate summit.

    In a recent development, I am still in awe of Francis, a community leader from Solomon Islands who traveled to Antalya to share his story. “Walande… the birthplace written in my passport, no longer exists,” he told a hushed room. “It is submerged beneath the waves.” His words moved the high-level event’s moderator to tears.

    Recent findings suggest that COP31’s inability to reach an overarching agreement leaves communities like Walande—and hundreds of other communities that have been forced to relocate—to face consequences of the climate crisis on their own. Despite coordinated calls from civil society, related outcome decisions do not include explicit discussion of displacement and planned relocation, and governments failed to increase funding to help frontline communities adapt. Nor was there recognition of the International Court of Justice’s landmark opinion affirming that governments have human rights obligations to address the climate crisis.

    Sources indicate that I leave Antalya holding both heartbreak and hope: the summit remains a vital space for global solidarity. Alongside partners in the Coalition on Dignified Climate Relocation, we brought frontline leaders, policymakers, and funders together to exchange lessons, and push for rights-respecting national policies and increased funding for communities forced to relocate. After watching our immersive documentary Solwata, several government officials and climate fund directors stepped up, committing to support finance and policies for relocating communities.

    Official negotiations fell woefully short, and the UN policy process failed to meet the moment in Antalya. But Marshall Islands, Bangladesh, Fiji, Nepal and other forward-thinking governments are proving that another path is possible. Dignified, rights-respecting solutions already exist—and they can be scaled up.

    Ethiopia, as host of COP32, should learn lessons from Australia and Türkiye’s failures, and center efforts to advance finance for adaptation and loss damage which are vital to protect the rights of climate displaced communities.

    The Persecution of Environmentalists and Indigenous Leaders in Indonesia.

    Climate Change, Planned Relocation, and People with Disabilities in Siargao, Philippines.

    A Pro-Life Progress Report for the 119th Congress and the Administration

    ⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that four years ago, the Supreme Court corrected a grave legal error and overturned Roe v.
    • Industry observers note that four years ago, the Supreme Court corrected a grave legal error and overturned Roe v.
    • From appropriations to the reconciliation process, the 119th Congress protected taxpayers from supporting abortion and abortion businesses.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that four years ago, the Supreme Court corrected a grave legal error and overturned Roe v. Wade. With abortion no longer enshrined as a “right” in the Constitution, policymakers at all levels of government have stepped up to promote life in law, policy, and culture. For the first session of each upcoming Congress, The Heritage Foundation provides pro-life policy recommendations to Members and the presidential Administration. The following year, a progress report takes stock of what has been accomplished and what remains on the to-do list. Last year, President Donald Trump and a Republican majority in Congress took the reins. Heritage provided a pro-life policy road map of ways to reverse four years of President Joe Biden’s pro-abortion radicalism.[REF] Now, this Backgrounder analyzes legislative and administrative accomplishments and highlights additional ways the Administration and Congress can protect life.In CongressFrom appropriations to the reconciliation process, the 119th Congress protected taxpayers from supporting abortion and abortion businesses.LegislationCongress advanced key legislation to promote a culture of life.Defunding Massive Abortion. Congress’s signature pro-life victory in 2025 was the One Big Beautiful Bill (OBBB) budget reconciliation measure. It included a provision preventing abortion providers like Planned Parenthood from receiving Medicaid reimbursements for one year.[REF] Medicaid makes up most of Planned Parenthood’s annual federal funding sources. In 2025, more than 50 clinics closed their doors, and across the country Planned Parenthood clinics are feeling the financial strain.[REF] Some blue states have stepped in to try to supplement funding but this is not sustainable in the long run.[REF] Both Planned Parenthood and blue state Attorneys General went to court to try to block the defund provision from taking effect, but were ultimately unsuccessful.[REF] Congress holds the power of the purse, and nothing in the Constitution entitles the abortion industry to Americans’ hard-earned tax dollars. As discussed below under “More to Accomplish,” another reconciliation bill could allow the defunding provision to extend beyond the OBBB’s one-year time frame, which has already passed. Planned Parenthood and other large abortion providers became eligible to receive Medicaid funds again on July 4, 2026.[REF]Supporting Pregnant and Parenting Students. In January 2026, the House of Representatives passed the Pregnant Students’ Rights Act (H.R. 6359),[REF] which requires universities to provide pregnant women and girls with information about their rights, resources, and available accommodations.Pregnancy Resource Center Support. Also in January 2026, the House also passed the Supporting Pregnant and Parenting Women and Families Act (H.R. 6945),[REF] which provides statutory clarity that states can direct Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) funding to pregnancy resource centers that support mothers, families, and unborn children through services like counseling, material support, and education.Addressing Weaponization and Selective Enforcement. The House Judiciary Committee approved the FACE Act Repeal Act (H.R. 589)[REF] in June 2025. The bill is needed in light of intense weaponization by the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) under President Biden, which is also discussed below. The Freedom of Access to Clinic Entrances (FACE) Act[REF] was enacted in 1994 and prohibits physically obstructing, injuring, intimidating, or interfering with anyone “obtaining or providing reproductive health services.” Under President Biden, the DOJ deliberately targeted peaceful pro-life Americans while failing to vigorously enforce FACE Act protections that apply to churches and pregnancy centers, which faced increasing attacks following the Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade. Sufficient laws already exist at the state level to address criminal activity, so Congress should repeal the FACE Act once and for all.AppropriationsCongress stood firm to protect life via spending legislation.Maintaining Status Quo of Pro-Life Policies. House-passed appropriations legislation has incorporated numerous pro-life policy riders, such as the Hyde family of amendments that prohibit taxpayer funding for abortions in foreign and domestic programs. However, new pro-life policy riders are routinely stripped during negotiations between the House and Senate.[REF]Addressing Problematic Earmarks. In FY 2024, two hospitals that perform late-term abortion procedures received almost $2.5 million in federal funds via earmarks in that year’s Labor-HHS [U.S. Department of Health and Human Services] funding.[REF] Those were Senate earmarks; the House Labor–HHS subcommittee accepted no earmark requests for FY 2024 through FY 2026.[REF] For FY 2027, the House Appropriations Committee’s Labor–HHS subcommittee provided guidance for earmark requests.[REF] Among requirements going forward, entities that perform or promote abortions are not eligible. Entities that conduct research using embryonic stem cells obtained from an induced abortion, or human germline gene modification, are not eligible. And entities that facilitate sex-rejecting interventions are not eligible.In the Trump AdministrationThe Trump Administration played a significant role in advancing pro-life policies.Previous Executive Orders and PoliciesIn 2025, the Administration quickly acted on a host of policies, which are discussed in the 2025 Backgrounder.[REF] They include:An executive order to disentangle taxpayers from abortion funding.[REF]Reinstatement of the Protecting Life in Global Health Assistance policy, which disentangles foreign aid dollars from international nongovernmental organizations that perform or promote abortions.[REF] As discussed in the following section, the policy has since been expanded.Defunding of the United Nations Population Fund over its complicity with China’s coercive and inhumane population-control practices.[REF]Renewal of membership in the Geneva Consensus Declaration, a partnership of more than 40 countries committed to improving women’s health, protecting innocent life, and strengthening the family.[REF]Partial restoration of Title X family planning program funding to Oklahoma[REF] and Tennessee.[REF] These pro-life states were denied funding by the Biden Administration over their refusal to provide abortion counseling and referrals.Recission of a Department of Defense abortion travel policy that made travel and transportation allowances available to service members and their dependents for abortions.[REF]Rescission of Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) guidance that wrongly claimed that EMTALA requires doctors to perform elective abortions.[REF]Pro-Life Regulations, Executive Orders, and Other PoliciesOver the past year and a half, the Trump Administration has taken additional steps to promote life-affirming policies. These steps include:Taxpayer Funding for Abortions. In July 2025, the Department of Justice issued an opinion[REF] that the Hyde Amendment, which prohibits taxpayer dollars from paying for elective abortions, means that the HHS cannot spend taxpayer dollars to provide “ancillary services necessary to receive an abortion”—such as the Office of Refugee Resettlement providing transportation for women seeking an abortion. The HHS has said it is reviewing the relevant regulations and guidance.[REF]Abortion in Obamacare Aims. On December 9, 2025, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) issued guidance[REF] about Section 1303 of the Affordable Care Act’s abortion coverage accounting gimmick. Section 1303 requires insurers to collect a separate payment for certain abortion coverage in qualified health plans approved to be sold on the exchanges. Maryland and other pro-abortion states attempted to commandeer excess funds remaining in abortion surcharge accounts to establish grant programs to pay for additional abortion travel and elective abortions.[REF] The CMS clarified that the leftover funds belong to insurers—not states seeking to subsidize additional abortions.As discussed below under “More to Accomplish,” the CMS should re-matter the Section 1303 regulation from President Trump’s first term. In December 2019, the CMS adopted a rule[REF] interpreting that separate payments be just that—separate—and that issuers needed to comply with the letter and spirit of Obamacare requirements. The same has not been true under Presidents Barack Obama and Biden. The CMS should rescind the Biden rule and return to the rule in place during President Trump’s first term.Abortion at the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). On December 18, 2025, the DOJ issued an opinion[REF] that the Biden Administration overstepped its authority by issuing a regulation requiring abortion procedures, referrals, and counseling to veterans at VA medical facilities. The VA quickly issued a memorandum returning to pre-2022 policies that excluded abortion and abortion counseling.[REF] On December 31, the VA issued a final rule formally rescinding the 2022 Biden Administration rule that returned to the pre-2022 abortion exclusions.[REF]International Abortion Funding. In January 2026, the Trump Administration declared that it is further expanding life-affirming foreign aid policies. Since the 1980s the Mexico City Policy has required (under Republican Administrations) foreign nongovernmental organizations to certify that they will not perform or promote abortion as a condition of receiving U.S. family planning assistance. During President Trump’s first Administration, that policy was expanded to apply to more funding streams and called the Protecting Life in Global Health Assistance Policy. Now, under a new name. the Promoting Human Flourishing in Foreign Assistance (PHFFA) Policy has expanded to encompass abortion,[REF] radical gender ideology,[REF] and diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI)[REF] policies as well.Fetal Tissue Research. In January 2026, the National Institutes of Health (NIH) reinstated a policy from President Trump’s first term ending support for unethical and obsolete research using fetal tissue obtained from elective abortion. The prohibition applies to internal and external projects (such as grants to outside entities). [REF] The NIH can prioritize ethical alternatives instead.Planned Parenthood COVID-19 “Relief” Funding. In January 2026, the Small Business Administration (SBA) announced that it is reviewing whether Planned Parenthood affiliates improperly received more than $88 million in loans during the COVID-19 pandemic. The SBA is demanding that Planned Parenthood clinics either prove that they were eligible to receive Paycheck Protection Program loans or return the funding.[REF] During President Trump’s first term, the SBA preliminarily concluded that Planned Parenthood affiliates were not eligible to receive these loans that were meant to help small businesses, but the Biden Administration later forgave many of those loans.[REF]Department of Justice Weaponization. In April 2026, the DOJ issued an extensive report detailing how the DOJ under President Biden weaponized the FACE Act against pro-life Americans.[REF] The report concluded: (1) The DOJ violated Americans’ rights through biased enforcement; (2) the DOJ collaborated with pro-abortion organizations to track pro-life activists’ activity; (3) prosecutors repeatedly engaged in inappropriate conduct; (4) the DOJ sought harsher punishment for pro-life activists than for pro-abortion activists; and (5) the DOJ inappropriately tried to help a pro-abortion organization with an application for a grant.Reviewing Human Embryonic Stem Cell Research. In January 2026, the NIH announced a pause on submissions to the NIH Human Embryonic Stem Cell Registry and issued a request for information on ways to reduce—and potentially replace—current reliance on research using human embryonic stem cells.[REF]Pro-Life Budget Request for FY 2027. In April 2026, the Office of Management and Budget released its budget request for the upcoming fiscal year. The request includes long-standing provisions in current law, such as Hyde protections across multiple departments (foreign and domestic), conscience protections, and bioethics-related funding restrictions for certain research. Additional requests include protections separating foreign aid funding from organizations that perform or promote abortions, including additional conscience protections for medical trainees, stripping Planned Parenthood of any HHS funding, and ending funding for fetal tissue research.[REF] This proposal is a request and Congress will ultimately decide FY 2027 funding and dollar amounts. As with the FY 2026 request, the Administration demonstrated its strong commitment to pro-life policymaking throughout the government.Redirecting Teen Pregnancy Prevention Funding to Align with Pro-Family Priorities. In June 2026, the HHS canceled most federal Teen Pregnancy Prevention Program grants two years early, some of which had gone to comprehensive sex-education curricula taught by abortion providers like Planned Parenthood. The HHS opened new funding opportunities that will be available to grantees who align programming with the Administration’s priorities of sexual risk avoidance education and not encouraging, normalizing, or promoting sexual activity for minors.[REF]Conscience RightsThe Trump Administration is prioritizing enforcement of federal conscience protection laws. The HHS Office for Civil Rights (OCR) is ensuring that no person or organization is discriminated against over their convictions on abortion and gender ideology.In January 2026, the OCR announced a list of enforcement actions and policy changes, including:A notice of violation determining that the Illinois law requiring abortion referrals violates the Weldon and Coats–Snowe Amendments.[REF]A nationwide “Dear Colleague” letter summarizing federal health care conscience protections that the OCR is tasked with enforcing and reaffirming the Administration’s commitment to protect individuals and organizations from being discriminated against due to their sincere moral or religious convictions.[REF]Recission of Biden Administration guidance that wrongly claims that federal law on emergency medical care requires doctors to perform elective abortions.[REF]Recission of Biden Administration guidance that wrongly instructed pharmacies to stock and dispense dangerous abortion pills, even though pharmacies and pharmacists have a right to not violate their conscience by participating in abortion. Under President Biden, the HHS walked back part of this guidance after losing a court case to pharmacies challenging the guidance.[REF] Now the guidance has been rescinded entirely.[REF]Disavowal of[REF] the Biden Administration’s August 2021 decision to withdraw the Trump Administration’s 2020 Notice of Violation that California broke federal conscience rights law over its insurance coverage mandate for elective abortion.Disavowal of[REF] the Biden Administration’s July 2021 decision to withdraw the Trump Administration’s Notice of Violation that the University of Vermont Medical Center broke federal conscience rights law by requiring a health care professional to participate in an abortion procedure despite strong objection.In March 2026, the HHS announced that the OCR is investigating 13 states over possible violations of the Weldon Amendment, which states government cannot discriminate against health care entities that do not pay for or provide coverage of abortions.[REF] The states under investigation have abortion coverage requirements for plans sold in their respective jurisdictions.[REF]In May 2026, the HHS announced an additional reorganization within the OCR.[REF] The OCR is tasked with enforcing federal civil rights laws related to conscience, religious freedom, privacy, cybersecurity, and more. In 2018, during President Trump’s first term, the HHS created a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division within the OCR. Under President Biden, this division was shuttered and absorbed, with the Civil Rights Division, into the Policy Division.[REF] Rights of conscience and religious freedom are not “less than.” Restoring the Conscience and Religious Freedom Division will provide the OCR with the tools it needs to best serve all Americans and ensure that their fundamental rights are respected.More to AccomplishBoth Congress and the Administration have successfully advanced important pro-life policies, but there is still more work to do.In CongressDefunding Big Abortion, maintaining long-standing pro-life policy riders, and holding bad actors accountable must continue to be a priority.Planned Parenthood. Preventing Planned Parenthood and other abortion providers from receiving Medicaid reimbursements for one year was a signature accomplishment in the 2025 OBBB budget reconciliation package. Medicaid makes up most of Planned Parenthood’s federal funding sources. However, this defunding provision was the only one in the entire bill subject to a one-year time frame rather than the full 10 years to which the bill can apply. Planned Parenthood and other large abortion providers became eligible to receive Medicaid funds again on July 4, 2026.[REF] If Congress discusses another reconciliation bill, the defunding provision should be incorporated for the full 10-year time frame so that taxpayers do not have to continue funding abortion providers.Appropriations. Congress has continued to include long-standing riders like the Hyde Amendment and similar language in annual appropriations bills, prohibiting taxpayer dollars from paying for most abortions. But many other pro-life policies can be enacted via appropriations riders. From expanding conscience protections to reinstating commonsense safety protections for risky abortion pills, there is more that Congress should do to promote life in must-pass spending legislation.[REF]Oversight. Congress should continue to invoke its oversight and investigatory role to hold bad actors accountable and ensure that that pro-life priorities in the Administration are not sidelined. For example, in 2022, activists obtained the remains of five preemie-size unborn babies who had been aborted at a notorious Washington, DC, late-term abortion mill. According to expert testimony, these babies may have been aborted using the illegal partial-birth abortion technique. One baby was still in the amniotic sac and may have been born alive and left to die.[REF] Local authorities stonewalled questions from Congress and the press about any investigation of this activity. Pro-life activists and Members of Congress feared that the DC Office of the Chief Medical Examiner would destroy the five bodies, but in February 2024 it confirmed that it would not immediately do so.[REF] During a June 2025 hearing, then-Attorney General Pam Bondi indicated that there was an ongoing investigation.[REF]Demand FDA Action on Dangerous Abortion Drugs. Congress should continue demanding transparency from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on its long-promised comprehensive review of the abortion pill. It is abundantly clear that current FDA postmarketing safety policies are not adequately protecting women and children.[REF] In light of the politicized approval process that put this risky drug on the market in the first place, a complete and thorough review is long overdue. Leadership changes at the FDA should not slow down or deprioritize this important work. Individual members and congressional committees should continue emphasizing the dangers these drugs pose to women, girls, and unborn children.In the Trump AdministrationThe Trump Administration should rescind Biden-era regulations and policies that promoted abortion and sought to undermine the 2022 Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade. These include:Abortion Travel for Unaccompanied Illegal Alien Children (UACs). A senior Office of Refugee Resettlement official told The Daily Signal[REF] that the agency is working on reversing a Biden-era regulation allowing taxpayer-funded abortion travel for UACs.[REF] The changes were submitted to the Office of Management and Budget’s Regulatory Information Service Center in January 2026, but the updated regulation has not been formally proposed yet. The HHS should ensure that the rule advances quickly.A Privacy Regulation That Undercut Abuse Reporting. In June 2025, a federal court struck down[REF] most of a Biden Administration regulation that purported to strengthen protections for sensitive private health information, including information related to abortion. In reality, the rule improperly limited state child abuse reporting laws.[REF] The HHS should formally rescind the rule.The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission’s (EEOC) Wrongful Interpretation of the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act (PWFA). In 2024, the EEOC issued rulemaking interpreting the PWFA’s definition of “medical condition” related to pregnancy to include elective abortion, thus requiring employers to provide accommodations like time off from work to have an abortion or time off to recover from the procedure.[REF] Litigation related to the entire rule is ongoing. In May 2025, a federal court provided nationwide relief for employers who care deeply about the well-being of their employees (and their children, born and unborn) by vacating the elective abortion accommodation provision.[REF] The EEOC should clean up the mess and formally rescind its erroneous interpretation of the PWFA. Pro-life Members of Congress would not have supported this bipartisan bill if it empowered the federal bureaucracy to invent a requirement for abortion accommodations.A Rollback of a Conscience Protection Regulation from President Trump’s First Term. The Biden Administration partially rescinded[REF] President Trump’s 2019 rule about enforcing more than a dozen federal laws that protect conscience rights for individuals or entities that do not want to participate in or facilitate morally fraught procedures such as abortion.[REF] The Biden rule gutted the HHS Office for Civil Rights’ ability to adequately enforce conscience laws that protect Americans’ civil rights. The regulation from President Trump’s first term should be restored.Addressing Title X Family Planning Program Funds Used as a Slush Fund for the Abortion Industry. The Biden Administration rescinded a regulation from President Trump’s first term that required recipients to physically and financially separate all abortion activity from Title X activity and prohibited Title X projects from promoting or referring for abortion.[REF] The Biden regulation also required sites that do not offer a broad range of contraception to provide a prescription or referral. This created a new barrier for sites that offer fertility awareness-based methods (FABMs) but cannot in good conscience provide or refer for other methods. The Title X program should not be used as a slush fund for abortion providers. The Trump Administration should restore the regulation from President Trump’s first term.A Clean Up of Policies Concerning the Affordable Care Act’s (ACA) Nondiscrimination Provision. Among other things, Section 1557 of the ACA prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, age, disability, and sex in covered health programs or activities.[REF] Just weeks after the Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade, the Biden Administration moved to redefine conditions related to “sex” to include abortion, as the Obama Administration had also done in 2016. The Trump Administration should revive the abortion-related provisions of this regulation from President Trump’s first term, issued in 2020.[REF]Ensuring that Issuers Comply with ACA Abortion Rules. Thirteen states require plans sold on their marketplace to include coverage for abortion. Section 1303 of the ACA says that such plans cannot use federal funds (including premium tax credits and cost-sharing reductions) for elective abortions. Section 1303 also requires issuers to collect a separate payment from each enrollee for the abortion coverage portion and segregate those funds in separate allocation accounts solely used for abortion coverage. Plans are also required to provide notice to enrollees at the time of enrollment that the strategy includes abortion coverage. But under Presidents Obama and Biden, CMS policy was essentially an accounting gimmick that did not enforce the letter or spirit of the ACA. The CMS should re-issue the Section 1303 regulation from President Trump’s first term. That rule[REF] rightly required that separate payments be just that: separate.Stopping Elective Abortions in the Indian Health Service (IHS) Program. The Biden Administration issued a rule that weakens the prohibition on abortion funding within the IHS.[REF] Per the Hyde Amendment, federal funds cannot be used to pay for abortion except in very limited circumstances. Under the Biden rule, if Congress ever fails to include the Hyde Amendment in annual appropriations legislation, then the IHS would be able to fund elective abortions.Robustly Enforcing Federal Conscience Protection Laws. Laws like the Church, Coats–Snowe, and Weldon Amendments are meant to ensure that no one faces discrimination for declining to perform, participate in, or pay for an abortion in HHS-funded programs. Under previous Administrations that prioritized a radical pro-abortion agenda, conscience protection was not a priority. The Trump Administration is reversing that trend. The HHS and the OCR should continue to protect Americans from discrimination in federally funded programs. For example, a February 2026 letter to the HHS from Alliance Defending Freedom identifies 49 HHS-funded family medicine residency programs that, it says, violate federal conscience laws by requiring residents to participate in abortion training.[REF]Prioritizing Health and Safety at the FDA and Department of Justice, Not the Abortion Industry’s Bottom Line. The FDA should expeditiously conduct its long-promised review of the abortion drug mifepristone and revisit the dangerous drug’s approval. At a minimum it must restore commonsense safety protections like in-person evaluation and dispensing. To that end, the DOJ also has a role to play in addressing mail-order abortion pills. For starters, it should rescind the Biden-era memorandum[REF] about interpretation of the Comstock Act, which prohibits mailing any “article or thing designed, adapted, or intended for producing abortion.”[REF] As explained in a Heritage Foundation Legal Memorandum, the Office of Legal Counsel’s interpretation of Comstock is so narrow “that it would be virtually unenforceable…. The plain and ordinary meaning of [Comstock] unambiguously prohibits mailing abortion drugs.”[REF]Pro-Life Progress Is PossibleSlim Republican–Democrat margins in Congress left little room for error when it comes to any legislative priority, including pro-life policies. That is why tools like budget reconciliation and must-pass appropriations legislation are so critical to advancing protections for babies and mothers.The Trump Administration has steadily rolled back much of the damage wrought by the Biden Administration, but key priorities are still unfinished. With the President’s second term in full swing, pro-life Americans expect to see policymakers continue to deliver more meaningful protections for women, girls, and unborn babies.Melanie Israel is a Visiting Fellow in the Richard and Helen DeVos Center for Human Flourishing at The Heritage Foundation.

    Industry observers note that four years ago, the Supreme Court corrected a grave legal error and overturned Roe v. Wade. With abortion no longer enshrined as a “right” in the Constitution, policymakers at all levels of government have stepped up to promote life in law, policy, and culture. For the first session of each newly introduced Congress, The Heritage Foundation provides pro-life policy recommendations to Members and the presidential Administration. The following year, a progress report takes stock of what has been accomplished and what remains on the to-do list. Last year, President Donald Trump and a Republican majority in Congress took the reins. Heritage provided a pro-life policy road map of ways to reverse four years of President Joe Biden’s pro-abortion radicalism.[REF] Now, this Backgrounder analyzes legislative and administrative accomplishments and highlights additional ways the Administration and Congress can protect life.

    From appropriations to the reconciliation process, the 119th Congress protected taxpayers from supporting abortion and abortion businesses.

    Congress advanced notable legislation to promote a culture of life.

    Defunding Big Abortion. Congress’s signature pro-life victory in 2025 was the One Big Beautiful Bill (OBBB) budget reconciliation measure. It included a provision preventing abortion providers like Planned Parenthood from receiving Medicaid reimbursements for one year.[REF] Medicaid makes up most of Planned Parenthood’s annual federal funding sources. In 2025, more than 50 clinics closed their doors, and across the country Planned Parenthood clinics are feeling the financial strain.[REF] Some blue states have stepped in to try to supplement funding but this is not sustainable in the long run.[REF] Both Planned Parenthood and blue state Attorneys General went to court to try to block the defund provision from taking effect, but were ultimately unsuccessful.[REF] Congress holds the power of the purse, and nothing in the Constitution entitles the abortion industry to Americans’ hard-earned tax dollars. As discussed below under “More to Accomplish,” another reconciliation bill could allow the defunding provision to extend beyond the OBBB’s one-year time frame, which has already passed. Planned Parenthood and other large abortion providers became eligible to receive Medicaid funds again on July 4, 2026.[REF].

    Sources indicate that supporting Pregnant and Parenting Students. In January 2026, the House of Representatives passed the Pregnant Students’ Rights Act (H.R. 6359),[REF] which requires universities to provide pregnant women and girls with information about their rights, resources, and available accommodations.

    Industry observers note that pregnancy Resource Center Support. Also in January 2026, the House also passed the Supporting Pregnant and Parenting Women and Families Act (H.R. 6945),[REF] which provides statutory clarity that states can direct Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) funding to pregnancy resource centers that support mothers, families, and unborn children through services like counseling, material support, and education.

    According to recent reports, addressing Weaponization and Selective Enforcement. The House Judiciary Committee approved the FACE Act Repeal Act (H.R. 589)[REF] in June 2025. The bill is needed in light of intense weaponization by the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) under President Biden, which is also discussed below. The Freedom of Access to Clinic Entrances (FACE) Act[REF] was enacted in 1994 and prohibits physically obstructing, injuring, intimidating, or interfering with anyone “obtaining or providing reproductive health services.” Under President Biden, the DOJ deliberately targeted peaceful pro-life Americans while failing to vigorously enforce FACE Act protections that apply to churches and pregnancy centers, which faced increasing attacks following the Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade. Sufficient laws already exist at the state level to address criminal activity, so Congress should repeal the FACE Act once and for all.

    Congress stood firm to protect life via spending legislation.

    Maintaining Status Quo of Pro-Life Policies. House-passed appropriations legislation has incorporated numerous pro-life policy riders, such as the Hyde family of amendments that prohibit taxpayer funding for abortions in foreign and domestic programs. However, upcoming pro-life policy riders are routinely stripped during negotiations between the House and Senate.[REF].

    Addressing Problematic Earmarks. In FY 2024, two hospitals that perform late-term abortion procedures received almost $2.5 million in federal funds via earmarks in that year’s Labor-HHS [U.S. Department of Health and Human Services] funding.[REF] Those were Senate earmarks; the House Labor–HHS subcommittee accepted no earmark requests for FY 2024 through FY 2026.[REF] For FY 2027, the House Appropriations Committee’s Labor–HHS subcommittee provided guidance for earmark requests.[REF] Among requirements going forward, entities that perform or promote abortions are not eligible. Entities that conduct research using embryonic stem cells obtained from an induced abortion, or human germline gene modification, are not eligible. And entities that facilitate sex-rejecting interventions are not eligible.

    The Trump Administration played a significant role in advancing pro-life policies.

    In 2025, the Administration rapidly acted on a host of policies, which are discussed in the 2025 Backgrounder.[REF] They include:.

    In a recent development, over the past year and a half, the Trump Administration has taken additional steps to promote life-affirming policies. These steps include:.

    It has been revealed that the Trump Administration is prioritizing enforcement of federal conscience protection laws. The HHS Office for Civil Rights (OCR) is ensuring that no person or organization is discriminated against over their convictions on abortion and gender ideology.

    In January 2026, the OCR announced a list of enforcement actions and policy changes, including:.

    In March 2026, the HHS announced that the OCR is investigating 13 states over possible violations of the Weldon Amendment, which states government cannot discriminate against health care entities that do not pay for or provide coverage of abortions.[REF] The states under investigation have abortion coverage requirements for aims sold in their respective jurisdictions.[REF].

    It has been revealed that in May 2026, the HHS confirmed an additional reorganization within the OCR.[REF] The OCR is tasked with enforcing federal civil rights laws related to conscience, religious freedom, privacy, cybersecurity, and more. In 2018, during President Trump’s first term, the HHS created a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division within the OCR. Under President Biden, this division was shuttered and absorbed, with the Civil Rights Division, into the Policy Division.[REF] Rights of conscience and religious freedom are not “less than.” Restoring the Conscience and Religious Freedom Division will provide the OCR with the tools it needs to best serve all Americans and ensure that their fundamental rights are respected.

    Both Congress and the Administration have successfully advanced key pro-life policies, but there is still more work to do.

    Defunding Substantial Abortion, maintaining long-standing pro-life policy riders, and holding bad actors accountable must continue to be a priority.

    Planned Parenthood. Preventing Planned Parenthood and other abortion providers from receiving Medicaid reimbursements for one year was a signature accomplishment in the 2025 OBBB budget reconciliation package. Medicaid makes up most of Planned Parenthood’s federal funding sources. However, this defunding provision was the only one in the entire bill subject to a one-year time frame rather than the full 10 years to which the bill can apply. Planned Parenthood and other large abortion providers became eligible to receive Medicaid funds again on July 4, 2026.[REF] If Congress discusses another reconciliation bill, the defunding provision should be incorporated for the full 10-year time frame so that taxpayers do not have to continue funding abortion providers.

    Recent findings suggest that appropriations. Congress has continued to include long-standing riders like the Hyde Amendment and similar language in annual appropriations bills, prohibiting taxpayer dollars from paying for most abortions. But many other pro-life policies can be enacted via appropriations riders. From expanding conscience protections to reinstating commonsense safety protections for risky abortion pills, there is more that Congress should do to promote life in must-pass spending legislation.[REF].

    According to recent reports, oversight. Congress should continue to invoke its oversight and investigatory role to hold bad actors accountable and ensure that that pro-life priorities in the Administration are not sidelined. For example, in 2022, activists obtained the remains of five preemie-size unborn babies who had been aborted at a notorious Washington, DC, late-term abortion mill. According to expert testimony, these babies may have been aborted using the illegal partial-birth abortion technique. One baby was still in the amniotic sac and may have been born alive and left to die.[REF] Local authorities stonewalled questions from Congress and the press about any investigation of this activity. Pro-life activists and Members of Congress feared that the DC Office of the Chief Medical Examiner would destroy the five bodies, but in February 2024 it confirmed that it would not immediately do so.[REF] During a June 2025 hearing, then-Attorney General Pam Bondi indicated that there was an ongoing investigation.[REF].

    It has been revealed that demand FDA Action on Dangerous Abortion Drugs. Congress should continue demanding transparency from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on its long-promised comprehensive review of the abortion pill. It is abundantly clear that current FDA postmarketing safety policies are not adequately protecting women and children.[REF] In light of the politicized approval process that put this risky drug on the market in the first place, a complete and thorough review is long overdue. Leadership changes at the FDA should not slow down or deprioritize this key work. Individual members and congressional committees should continue emphasizing the dangers these drugs pose to women, girls, and unborn children.

    Recent findings suggest that the Trump Administration should rescind Biden-era regulations and policies that promoted abortion and sought to undermine the 2022 Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade. These include:.

    Sources indicate that slim Republican–Democrat margins in Congress left little room for error when it comes to any legislative priority, including pro-life policies. That is why tools like budget reconciliation and must-pass appropriations legislation are so critical to advancing protections for babies and mothers.

    The Trump Administration has steadily rolled back much of the damage wrought by the Biden Administration, but key priorities are still unfinished. With the President’s second term in full swing, pro-life Americans expect to see policymakers continue to deliver more meaningful protections for women, girls, and unborn babies.

    Melanie Israel is a Visiting Fellow in the Richard and Helen DeVos Center for Human Flourishing at The Heritage Foundation.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Virginia, by Judge Toby Heytens, joined by Judge DeAndrea Gist Benjamin:.
    • Sources indicate that [W]e vacate a preliminary injunction preventing the Commonwealth of Virginia from rendering unenforceable existing agreements between the Federal Government and the Commonwealth's state or local agencies "to perform [the] function[s] of a federal immigration officer" unless certain conditions are met.
    • It also does not violate the Federal Constitution's Contracts Clause for two separate reasons: (1) because the existing agreements all expressly permit the non-federal party to unilaterally terminate without cause; and (2) even if they did not, the Commonwealth would have constitutionally valid justifications for imposing upcoming terms for future cooperation in any event….
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    From today's decision in U.S. v. Virginia, by Judge Toby Heytens, joined by Judge DeAndrea Gist Benjamin:.

    Sources indicate that [W]e vacate a preliminary injunction preventing the Commonwealth of Virginia from rendering unenforceable existing agreements between the Federal Government and the Commonwealth's state or local agencies "to perform [the] function[s] of a federal immigration officer" unless certain conditions are met. The Federal Government may not "command" the Commonwealth's "officers, or those of [its] political subdivisions" (Printz v. U.S. (1997)) to assist with federal immigration enforcement efforts, and the Commonwealth's supreme lawmaking body has imposed new limits on when its agents may agree to do so. That choice does not violate the intergovernmental immunity doctrine because it neither requires the Federal Government to do anything nor limits any private party's ability to contract with the Federal Government.

    It also does not violate the Federal Constitution's Contracts Clause for two separate reasons: (1) because the existing agreements all expressly permit the non-federal party to unilaterally terminate without cause; and (2) even if they did not, the Commonwealth would have constitutionally valid justifications for imposing upcoming terms for future cooperation in any event….

    Sources indicate that [But] we affirm a preliminary injunction forbidding enforcement of a upcoming state law that regulates when federal employees may wear facial coverings and must display visible identification while performing their federal duties…. [J]ust as Congress may not "issue orders directly to the States," States may not issue orders directly to the Federal Government. We thus conclude the law at issue violates the intergovernmental immunity doctrine….

    Sources indicate that our holding is limited. We reiterate that "an employee of the United States does not secure a general immunity from state law while acting in the course of his employment," and we make no effort to provide a full list of situations in which federal officers may or may not be prosecuted for violating state law.

    We also emphasize that neither the Federal Government's broad authority in immigration matters, nor "the history and context for the enactment of" the Mask/Identity Law play any role in our analysis. Whether the Mask/Identity Law directly regulates the Federal Government does not depend on what motivated the Commonwealth's decision to enact the law or whether its various provisions (or the practices that prompted them) represent wise policy.

    Finally, we do not address whether other legal requirements—including the Fourth Amendment—limit the permissible use of masked and otherwise-unidentified law enforcement officers….

    According to recent reports, judge Robert King agreed with the majority as to the likely validity of Virginia's refusal to assist with immigration enforcement, but dissented as to the mask/identity statute. For the full (long) opinions, see here.

    Industry observers note that veterans Day is more than a commemoration of military service. It is also a reminder that freedom depends on citizens willing to serve something larger than themselves—and not just when they are in uniform.

    Our service members do much more than most of us realize, and our society is the better for it.

    Recent findings suggest that across generations, American veterans have answered the nation’s call in war and peace out of a commitment to duty, sacrifice and country. Their example shows that citizenship carries responsibilities as well as rights, and that self-government endures only when citizens place the common good above personal interest.

    According to recent reports, the freedoms that Americans enjoy today were secured by all veterans who served. They defended not merely our borders but also the principles upon which this nation was founded: liberty, representative government and the rule of law.

    Recent findings suggest that by defending the constitutional order, veterans helped preserve a nation in which political differences are settled through lawful debate and elections rather than force. Veterans Day is an opportunity to recognize the men and women whose sacrifices have made that peaceful self-government possible.

    >>> The Three Values That Are the Real Keys to America’s Greatness.

    Sources indicate that veterans have helped secure liberty against some of the most oppressive ideologies in human history, including communism and national socialism. American veterans were instrumental in defeating the Nazi regime during World War II, helping liberate Europe from a government built on tyranny, aggression and the systematic denial of human freedom.

    During the Cold War, generations of American servicemen and women stood watch against the expansion of Soviet communism, preserving the security of the free world through deterrence and steadfast resolve. Their service helped create the conditions that led to the collapse of the Soviet Union and the liberation of millions of people in Central and Eastern Europe.

    The freedom enjoyed today by nations once trapped behind the Iron Curtain is part of the legacy of those veterans who answered their country’s call.

    In a recent development, across these conflicts, American veterans served as guardians of the principle that free people have the right to govern themselves. Veterans Day also reminds us that liberty is never self-executing. The constitutional freedoms secured through military sacrifice endure only when citizens practice the discipline, responsibility and respect for law that self-government requires.

    The veteran’s example therefore reaches beyond the battlefield, offering a model for preserving freedom in civic life.

    Industry observers note that veterans also participate in freedom’s defense at home at some of the highest rates in American society. According to the 2025 Veterans Civic Health Index, 81% of veterans were registered to vote in the 2024 election, compared with 74% of nonveterans. Seventy-three percent of veterans cast ballots, compared with 66% of nonveterans.

    The index also reports stronger veteran participation in volunteering, in civic organizations and in engagement with public officials and community institutions. Together, these measures point to a broader pattern: For many veterans, military service becomes a lifelong commitment to citizenship, civic responsibility and the preservation of our constitutional republic.

    Veterans continue to serve as teachers, business leaders, first responders, elected officials and civic volunteers, bringing military habits of integrity, discipline and teamwork into civilian life. At Military.com, Medal of Honor recipient Clint Romesha captures that enduring impulse, saying, “So many of us veterans just want to continue to serve after service.”.

    In a recent development, mr. Romesha identifies teamwork as one of the military’s greatest lessons—“It’s not about me; it’s about the team”—and as a principle that continues to guide veterans long after they leave the uniform behind.

    Industry observers note that the veteran profiles of “American Heroes: Stories of Service” and “Pledge to Patriots” show this continuing commitment in action. These stories feature veterans mentoring young people, supporting one another, leading nonprofits, responding to disasters and strengthening communities.

    >>> Nina and the Bikers.

    In a recent development, thousands of veterans serve as poll workers, election officials and observers, helping to administer and safeguard elections. As a former election official and U.S. Navy veteran, I have seen them step forward when communities need poll workers. Through the nonpartisan Vet the Vote initiative, more than 163,000 veterans and military family members served as poll workers during the 2024 election cycle, up from approximately 63,500 during the 2022 midterms.

    National Guard members have supported election operations, security, coordination and emergency response at the request of state authorities. Their commitment to duty, adherence to procedures and record of public service can strengthen confidence in the electoral process they defended in uniform.

    According to recent reports, on Veterans Day, we honor those who wore the uniform in defense of our nation. We should also follow the example they continue to set—as citizens, poll workers, community leaders and public servants—reminding us that freedoms secured on far-off battlefields must be preserved through faithful participation in self-government at home.

    Veterans Day recognizes a profound commitment to country, but it also challenges every American to accept the duties of citizenship.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that (London) – Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Hindu nationalist government has systematically weakened institutions established to protect human rights and democratic freedoms, Human Rights Watch said in a report released today. Indians have increasingly taken to the streets to protest government repression, corruption, and a deeply flawed revision of voter lists.

    It has been revealed that the 95-page report, “‘So What’s This Democracy We’re Talking About?’: Modi’s Authoritarian Playbook in India,” finds that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led government is undermining parliamentary procedures, suppressing the political opposition, and weaponizing federal investigative agencies for political ends. Human Rights Watch found that the government is also weakening constitutional and statutory bodies, such as the Election Commission, Central Information Commission, the anti-corruption ombudsman, and human rights commissions, and interfering in the judicial branch.

    Modi’s Authoritarian Playbook in India.

    Download the full report in English.

    It has been revealed that “Over the past decade, the Modi government has been hollowing out India’s independent institutions that are critical to checking executive power and protecting civil liberties,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “The government has eroded the rule of law and promoted Hindu majoritarianism, rolling back human rights protections, undermining the rights of marginalized communities, and deepening India’s authoritarian slide.”.

    Human Rights Watch interviewed over 40 lawyers, journalists, activists, researchers, academics, current and former judges, and former government officials between January 2025 and September 2026.

    Industry observers note that the Modi administration has frequently disregarded parliamentary oversight mechanisms to impose its political agenda. In December 2023, the government adopted a law that entrenched executive control over the appointment of election commissioners and granted them sweeping legal immunity for actions, decisions, or statements made while carrying out their official duties. The law was passed even as opposition members were suspended in unprecedented numbers from both houses for the entire session of the parliament, 100 from Lok Sabha (the House of the People or lower house) and 46 from Rajya Sabha (the Council of States or upper house).

    In a recent development, the BJP did not have a majority in the Rajya Sabha from 2014 to 2024. While all bills must be approved by both houses to become law, some regulating financial matters can be introduced in the Lok Sabha as “money bills,” which do not require Rajya Sabha approval. The Modi administration aggressively used money bills to push through laws with serious consequences for fundamental rights that would not qualify as money bills.

    In a recent development, in 2019, the government used this approach to amend the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, significantly expanding the authority of the Enforcement Directorate, the federal enforcement agency it has used to improperly target political opponents, activists, and critics. The expansion of Enforcement Directorate powers would not appear to fall within the parameters set out for a money bill.

    The Election Commission has repeatedly failed to hold Modi and senior BJP leaders to account despite apparent violations of the election code of conduct by use of hate speech. The commission has also failed to credibly investigate allegations by voters, activists, academics, and political parties of manipulation of registered voter lists, suppression of polling data, irregularities in counting votes, or interfering with voting machines.

    Industry observers note that the commission is right now facing a massive crisis of credibility amid concerns over its ability to function independent of the executive. A Special Intensive Revision, purportedly to delete dead, duplicate, or ineligible voters, has arbitrarily removed over 130 million names from electoral rolls since June 2025, sparking nationwide protests in October 2026.

    Sources indicate that the administration has used federal agencies to pressure members of rival parties to defect to the BJP. After amending the law against money laundering, official data shows that the Enforcement Directorate filed cases against 193 politicians between April 2015 and February 2025, most of whom were government opponents. This was more than a 600 percent jump from the 26 politicians investigated in the decade preceding the Modi administration. Such investigations are promptly stalled, or charges are dropped if the accused switches loyalties, leading opposition parties to call the BJP a “washing machine.”.

    The Modi government has since 2014 increasingly used federal investigation agencies to target domestic and international rights groups, human rights lawyers, activists, and media organizations under the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act and other laws dealing with financial irregularities. It has used the abusive counterterrorism law, the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), to wrongfully jail human rights activists, journalists, students, peaceful protesters, academics, and critics, sometimes for years without trial.

    It has been revealed that india’s courts have also failed to uphold fundamental freedoms. In 2022, the Supreme Court endorsed and expanded the authority of enforcement agencies for arrest and search and seizure under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. Legal scholars criticized the verdict as gutting rights to life and liberty.

    Sources indicate that the Supreme Court is currently hearing petitions regarding the legitimacy of the electoral roll revision process. In May 2026, even after millions of names had been eliminated from voter lists, the court ruled that the data did not indicate “systemic disenfranchisement.” In April, after 9 million names—12 percent of the electorate—in West Bengal state had been removed, the court effectively said it was acceptable for them not to vote at that time so long as they would be added back to the rolls. Shortly afterward, the BJP won control of the state for the first time. By November, the Election Commission, after protests, started reversing some of the decisions that had led to the arbitrary removal of names.

    The Modi administration’s actions over the past decade are not isolated institutional failures but mutually reinforcing elements of an authoritarian playbook, Human Rights Watch mentioned. A weakened opposition has fewer means to resist laws that entrench executive control. Institutions led by political appointees, such as the federal and state human rights commissions, have not adequately responded to efforts to prevent the silencing of civil society. When courts fail to provide timely and effective remedies, these abuses go unchecked.

    India’s allies should publicly and privately raise concerns about ongoing abuses and the deterioration of democratic institutions, including during high-level engagements and interactions, at the United Nations Human Rights Council, and in negotiations for bilateral trade and security agreements.

    According to recent reports, “Checking India’s democratic decline means ending the use of state institutions as weapons against government critics and rebuilding them as safeguards for everyone’s rights,” Pearson remarked. “India’s allies should press the Modi government to end its assault on independent institutions and restore checks on executive power.”.

    Education policymakers around the world often overlook a simple formula: To increase educational opportunity, increase economic development.

    According to recent reports, but to improve development, a country needs the institutions that promote it. That’s why nations that want to help more children succeed should pursue economic freedom.

    The latest Economic Freedom of the World report from the Fraser Institute tells the story clearly. The highest-ranked 25% of countries for economic freedom dramatically outperform the lowest-ranked 25%. Incomes are seven times greater, while people work six fewer hours per week. People live 14 years longer. Fewer children die in infancy, and environments are cleaner.

    Economic freedom translates into education and economic opportunity. Fewer students in developing nations will drop out in middle school to go to work. More families will be able to afford transportation to school. There will be more opportunities for graduates to get more productive, higher-paying jobs.

    >>> Latin America Shifts Toward Market-Oriented Conservatism.

    Sources indicate that take, for instance, Kurdistan in Iraq, which is focusing more on education now. Iraq ranks 159 out of 165 countries for its legal system and property rights, 152 for size of government, 141 for sound money, 149 for regulation of the economy, and 129 for freedom to trade internationally.

    Imagine how many more students in Kurdistan could finish school with a great education if incomes were seven times higher. Imagine the hard trade-offs today that would not be necessary if Iraq were richer.

    Sources indicate that this point holds worldwide. What would best help a country’s children receive a strong education in the long run? Focus first of all on the country’s economic and legal institutions.

    According to recent reports, education is about making intends for society’s future. That means a small government with reliable courts, sound money, secure property rights, and free competition.

    Economic development doesn’t automatically mean more government funding for government schools. In many countries, it can mean trusting families with education dollars to choose what is best for their own children.

    According to recent reports, indeed, parents are a great education resource. They are the first line of influence to keep their children on track for success, and you don’t even have to pay them a salary.

    Governments can do more to consider how to empower parents and teachers. Families know their own children the best. Teachers know their own students as individuals far better than a national government or the United Nations or UNICEF could ever know them.

    It has been revealed that using international aid to push an ideological agenda is the wrong policy. Education policy choices should emphasize local knowledge rather than national and international one-size-fits-all, top-down impositions.

    >>> Stablecoins Strengthen the Dollar and Empower the Developing World.

    Educators also should teach economic and financial literacy. The scientific evidence is decisive that socialism fails and market economies succeed. We mark Nov. 7 each year as Victims of Communism Day in the United States by remembering the more than 100 million people who died of starvation or were killed under communist and socialist regimes in the 20th century.

    Recent findings suggest that on an individual level, each student should be taught the basics of economics and entrepreneurship. These lessons include the fundamentals of human action and incentives, supply and demand, and the invisible hand of Adam Smith. This also includes learning how to be alert to opportunities to create value for others in society while improving one’s own life.

    This education means respecting and admiring entrepreneurs. Students should understand why people should be allowed to keep the fruit of their own labor. Students also should understand the value of building capital rather than consumption if they want to prosper.

    According to recent reports, to prepare students for employment and participation in society, teach economics and inspire entrepreneurship and an entrepreneurial mindset. Then the next generation will better understand the institutional reforms needed to help their country thrive.

    It has been revealed that given the results of the latest U.S. election, now that newly introduced policymakers with socialist leanings (and actual socialists) will govern in states such as Michigan, New York, California, and elsewhere starting next year, this advice is not just for other countries. It’s also for us. Will we listen?
